items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to property tax benefits for anaerobic digestion of agricultural waste; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5809

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to property tax
benefits for anaerobic digestion of agricultural waste; and to repeal
certain provisions of such law relating thereto

PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to amend the Real Property Tax Law (RPTL)
to clearly provide property tax benefits for anaerobic digestion of
agriculturally derived feedstocks that provide manure management and
renewable energy generation for use by a farm and/or for sale through
the grid; and to repeal those portions of RPTL § 487 that apply to
farm waste energy systems to remove confusion with the previously
amended RPTL § 483-a.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends RPTL § 483-a to include language that
clearly allows for the sale of the energy generated by an anaerobic
digester through the grid (off-site) or to a farm (on-site), without
jeopardizing the tax exempt status of the anaerobic digester, the
equipment used to process the waste to energy and the property it is
located upon. The amendment includes the removal of the word
"agricultural" in reference to the land on which a digester is affixed
to ensure the tax exemption even if the land is zoned as other than
agricultural.

Section 2 of the bill repeals the definitions of "farm waste electric
generating equipment" and "farm waste energy system" in RPTL § 487 to
remove confusion with the newly amended RPTL § 483-a.

Section 3 of the bill amends the definition of "incremental cost" in
paragraph (d) of subdivision 1 of RPTL § 487 to remove references to
farm waste energy systems.

Section 4 of the bill amends the section heading and subdivisions 2,
3, 4, 5 and 8 of RPTL § 487 to remove references to farm waste energy
equipment and systems.

Section 5 of the bill provides the effective date.

EXISTING LAW:

In 2013, the Legislature passed S. 4770-A/ A. 7982 (Gallivan/Magee)
(Chapter 272 of the Laws of 2013) clarifying that composting and
anaerobic digestion of agricultural materials are entitled to a real
property tax exemption as "manure storage, handling and treatment
facilities" under RPTL § 483-a.

The Courts have since ruled that the existence of similar language is
RPTL § 487 is confusing and therefore have allowed the municipality of
Covington, NY (Wyoming County) to tax an anaerobic digester as Energy
Generation, an outcome unintended by previous legislation.


JUSTIFICATION:

In 2013, the Legislature passed S 4770-A/ A. 7982 (Gallivan/Magee)
(Chapter 272 of the Laws of 2013) clarifying that composting and
anaerobic digestion of agricultural materials are entitled to a real
property tax exemption as "manure storage, handling and treatment
facilities" under RPTL § 483-a.

Expanding the implementation of anaerobic digesters has also been
priority of Governor Cuomo as he affirmed at the NYS Yogurt Summit
held in August of 2012, where he stated "We, as an administration,
want to encourage digesters."

Anaerobic digestion of livestock manure and other agriculturally
derived organic materials provides multiple environmental benefits
including: water quality protection, air quality improvement,
reduction of greenhouse gases, energy efficiency benefits, public
health protection, natural resource conservation, solid waste
reduction and renewable energy generation. While the benefits are
many, farmers have been slow to adopt this technology due to the high
capital costs and tight financial margins of anaerobic digestion.

To be eligible for tax benefits at least fifty percent by weight of
the anaerobic digester feedstock on an annual basis must consist of
livestock manure, farming wastes or crops grown specifically for use
as anaerobic digestion feedstock. This standard ensures that such
facilities maintain an important direct connection to farm operations,
helping them with critical nutrient management needs. The RPTL should
be revised and updated to include anaerobic digesters as integral
parts of agricultural manure management systems.

In light of the changes already made to RPTL § 483-a, which make
anaerobic digestion of agricultural materials eligible for a real
property tax exemption, the farm waste energy tax exemption in RPTL
487 is no longer needed Since any on-farm digester seeking a property
tax exemption will use § 483-a, keeping the § 487 exemption would be
confusing. That confusion could lead other municipalities to tax
anaerobic digesters as Energy Generation, potentially bankrupting
existing digesters and discouraging the development of new digesters
in New York State.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill. It clarifies Chapter 272 of the Laws of 2013 to
state that composting and anaerobic digestion of agricultural
materials are entitled to a real property tax exemption as "manure
storage, handling and treatment facilities" under RPTL § 483-a.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state. This bill clarifies existing state law. The
clarification will prevent the taxing of anaerobic digesters as energy
generation, potentially bankrupting existing digesters and
discouraging the development of new digesters in New York State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:


Immediately, and shall apply to the taxable year of 2013 and
thereafter.
